title: What is known about 1RB1LE_0RC0RA_0RD1RF_1LD1LA_0LA0LE_0LB---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LE_0RC0RA_0RD1RF_1LD1LA_0LA0LE_0LB---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The tape is a list of numbers that each sweep translates between two codes: long runs of 0s (up to 52) between short groups like (10)^3 1 1 when the head is at the left end, long runs of 1s (up to 46) between 0 0 or 0 (01)^k when it is at the right end. Measured, not proved. Halting needs F on a 1, entered only from C on a 1; F has always found a 0.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 47,586 cells have been visited and 26,786 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.154). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.516).

claims.title: Shift rules of the sweeps
claims.text: Lean proves, for every count and every tape around, the shift rules of the sweeps: A crosses (10)^n leftward and B crosses it rightward, both turning it into (01)^n, and E crosses (01)^n leftward turning it into (10)^n; 2 steps per copy.

claims.title: Two codes for one list
claims.text: At the last left extension before 109 steps (step 832,384,202) the runs of 1s are at most 7 long and the runs of 0s up to 52, e.g. A>0 0 1 0 1^3 (01)^4 1^6 0^9 (10)^3 1^3 (01)^3 …; at the last right extension (step 996,208,311) the runs of 0s are at most 2 long and the runs of 1s up to 46: 1^12 00 1^23 00 1^8 0 (01)^6 1^14 0 (01)^8 1^11 ….

claims.title: Never one step from a halt
claims.text: The machine halts when F reads a 1, and F is entered only from C reading a 1 (C1 → 1RF). In the first 3·10<sup>6</sup> steps C reads a 1 106,723 times, always with a 0 to its right.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The two forms are measured; the map a sweep makes on the list is not written down, and the list looks irregular, so this may be a chaotic machine.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine rewrites its whole tape on every sweep, turning long runs of 0s into long runs of 1s and back. This page shows the two forms and what is proved.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 47,586 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: Runs of 0s become runs of 1s
html: With the head at the left end the tape is long runs of 0s between short groups:
With the head at the right end, long runs of 1s between short groups:
(0^9 is nine 0s, (01)^6 is 01 six times.) Each sweep translates the whole list from one form to the other. No order in the numbers has been found.

sections.heading: What a halt would need
html: The machine stops only in F reading a 1, and F is entered only from C reading a 1 (moving right). So a halt needs C on a 1 followed by a 1. In the first 3·106 steps C reads a 1 106,723 times and the next cell is always 0. Open.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.154). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.516).
After 109 steps the tape spans 47,586 cells (1,358 left of the start, 33,799 right), with a density of 1s of 0.563.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: list of numbers rewritten between two codes (runs of 0s and runs of 1s)
summary: Every sweep rewrites the tape between two codes: at the left end the numbers are long runs of 0s between short groups of 1s, at the right end they are long runs of 1s between short groups of 0s; the numbers look irregular.
